title: Hex dump
description:
A memory view shows bytes as pairs of hexadecimal digits. Write the function behind one.

`hexDump(data, size)` is given the address of some memory and a number of bytes. It returns those bytes as text: two capital hex digits each, with a single space between bytes and none at the end.

For `int score{ 1000 };` the call `hexDump(&score, sizeof(score))` returns `"E8 03 00 00"`. That is the little-endian layout from the last lesson, read straight out of memory.

A size of 0 gives an empty string.

`data` is a `const void*`, an address with no type attached. To read bytes through it, convert it to a `const unsigned char*`.
hints: Start with `const auto* bytes{ static_cast<const unsigned char*>(data) };`. Now `bytes` points at the same memory, seen as individual bytes.
One byte is two hex digits. `byte / 16` is the first digit and `byte % 16` is the second, each a number from 0 to 15.
Look each digit up in the string `"0123456789ABCDEF"`. Use `unsigned char` for the byte: a plain `char` can be negative, and a negative index would read the wrong place.
Add the space **before** every byte except the first. That way there is never one left over at the end.
rules: Build the hex digits yourself, as in the last lesson.
